finding.claim: Unauthenticated /preview fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL with no validation. An attacker can reach internal services, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) and other non-public hosts. The response status and the first 500 characters of the body are returned, so this is full-read SSRF. requests also follows redirects, and file:// is not supported by requests, but any http(s) scheme is.
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:16; the response is reflected via jsonify at app.py:17

trace.note: target = request.args.get('url', '') takes the attacker-controlled query parameter
target passed unmodified to requests.get (redirects followed by default)
status code and resp.text[:500] returned to the caller, so the response is visible to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: None. There is no scheme check, host allowlist, resolved-IP check or redirect restriction. The route has no authentication.

verdict.guard_found: none (the ALLOWED_HOSTS check exists only in /partner at app.py:23-25, not in /preview; no auth or middleware)
verdict.reason: app.py:15 reads the attacker-controlled 'url' query param and app.py:16 passes it unvalidated to requests.get, with status and the first 500 chars of the body returned at app.py:17; the host allowlist at app.py:24 applies only to /partner.

finding.claim: /partner has a hostname allowlist, but it is weak. The check runs on urlparse(target).hostname (a pre-DNS string check), and the original unmodified string is then fetched by requests/urllib3, a different parser. This is a validator/fetcher parser-differential surface. requests.get also follows redirects by default (allow_redirects=True), so any open redirect or attacker-influenced redirect on an allowlisted host (api.partner.example or cdn.partner.example) bounces the server to an arbitrary internal target. The redirect target is never re-validated. Only the status code is returned, so this is a blind or limited-read SSRF. Confidence is lower than ssrf-1, because exploitation needs a redirect on an allowlisted host or a parser differential that I did not confirm against the installed urllib3 version.

trace.note: target = request.args.get('url') takes the attacker-controlled query parameter
host = urlparse(target).hostname is parsed with urllib.parse (parser P1)
host checked against ALLOWED_HOSTS. Only the hostname string is compared; scheme, port and the resolved IP are not checked
the original target string is passed to requests.get (parser P2 = urllib3) with redirects followed automatically

finding.guards_checked: Exact-match hostname allowlist (ALLOWED_HOSTS) on urlparse().hostname. There is no scheme restriction, no re-validation after redirects, no allow_redirects=False, no DNS or resolved-IP pinning, and the URL is not rebuilt from parsed components. /health (app.py:32) was also checked and is not a finding: STATUS_URL comes from an environment variable and is not attacker-controlled.

verdict.guard_found: Exact hostname set membership: `host = urlparse(target).hostname` (app.py:23) checked with `host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS` (app.py:24-25) against a two-entry set (app.py:9).
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate and `url` is attacker-controlled (app.py:22), but app.py:23-25 applies exact set membership on the parsed hostname, which closes the finding; the redirect and parser-differential routes are unconfirmed speculation, and only the status code is returned (app.py:27).
